intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
experiences.description: One of New Zealand's most iconic day hikes, this 19.4km trek crosses an active volcanic landscape with emerald lakes, steaming vents, and panoramic views. Book a shuttle from Queenstown or Wanaka for an early morning start. Since your flight arrives late on Day 1, plan this for Day 2 or later when you are well-rested and settled near the trailhead.
experiences.location: Tongariro National Park, Central South Island

experiences.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungee Jump
experiences.description: The world's first commercial bungee jump site, located just 23km from Queenstown CBD. At 43 metres above the Kawarau River, this is the perfect introduction to bungee jumping. Stay in central Queenstown to be within easy reach of this iconic activity and avoid long transfers after your late arrival on Day 1.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy - New Zealand's Highest Bungee
experiences.description: A 134-metre freefall suspended above the Nevis River gorge, this is New Zealand's highest bungee jump and one of the most thrilling in the world. A dedicated bus departs from Queenstown town centre, making it easy to access if you are staying centrally. Schedule this mid-trip when you are fully acclimatised.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Day Hike
experiences.description: A world-renowned Great Walk offering stunning alpine scenery, beech forests, and views of the Darran Mountains. The day hike to Routeburn Falls and Lake Harris is achievable without a multi-day permit. Stay in Glenorchy or central Queenstown to minimise travel time to the trailhead and make the most of daylight hours.

experiences.name: Ben Lomond Summit Hike
experiences.description: A challenging full-day hike rising 1748 metres above sea level with sweeping 360-degree views over Queenstown, Lake Wakatipu, and the Remarkables. The trailhead is accessible directly from Queenstown town centre via the Skyline gondola or on foot, making it ideal if you are staying centrally. A perfect activity from Day 2 onwards once you have recovered from your late arrival.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Day Hike
experiences.description: A world-renowned Great Walk offering stunning alpine scenery, beech forests, and views of the Darran Mountains. The day hike to Routeburn Falls and Lake Harris is achievable without a multi-day permit. Stay in Glenorchy or central Queenstown to minimise travel time to the trailhead and make the most of daylight hours.

experiences.name: Ben Lomond Summit Hike
experiences.description: A challenging full-day hike rising 1748 metres above sea level with sweeping 360-degree views over Queenstown, Lake Wakatipu, and the Remarkables. The trailhead is accessible directly from Queenstown town centre via the Skyline gondola or on foot, making it ideal if you are staying centrally. A perfect activity from Day 2 onwards once you have recovered from your late arrival.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage and take the Orbus public bus (Route 1, ~$2–4 NZD) into Queenstown town centre. Check in to Queenstown Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely walk along the Queenstown lakefront promenade to get oriented. Enjoy the views of Lake Wakatipu and The Remarkables mountain range.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Queenstown town centre, browse the shops on Beach Street, and explore the buzzing atmosphere. Head to the iconic Fergburger for a budget-friendly but legendary Queenstown burger dinner.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport on arrival
meals.lunch: Pick up a meat pie or sandwich from a bakery near the bus stop or airport — around $5–8 NZD
meals.dinner: Fergburger on Shotover Street — burgers from $15–20 NZD, a Queenstown institution

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light to allow for rest after a long flight. Grab a Queenstown map from the i-SITE visitor centre near the waterfront. Buy an Orbus card to save on bus fares throughout your stay. Confirm your accommodation check-in time in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early start with the Ben Lomond Summit Hike. Depart from the Queenstown Gondola base on Brecon Street (walk from the hotel, ~10 minutes). Take the Tiki Trail up through native forest to the Ben Lomond Saddle, then push on to the 1,748m summit. Allow 5–7 hours total for the full hike. Pack lunch and plenty of water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach the summit and enjoy sweeping 360-degree panoramic views over Queenstown, Lake Wakatipu, The Remarkables, and the Dart Valley. Begin the descent back to town via the same trail. The descent takes approximately 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Rest tired legs back at the hotel. Head out for a casual dinner at a budget-friendly spot in town. Visit the Queenstown Night Market (held Thursdays–Sundays on Earl Street) if timing aligns for cheap, diverse street food options.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats or toast at the accommodation before departing — save money by buying basics from a supermarket (Countdown or New World on Gorge Road)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the Ben Lomond Saddle or summit — homemade sandwiches, trail mix, and fruit from the supermarket
meals.dinner: Vudu Café & Larder on Rees Street for affordable, wholesome meals (~$18–25 NZD) or grab a cheap kebab from one of the late-night spots on Shotover Street

day_by_day.notes: Ben Lomond is a strenuous hike — wear sturdy hiking boots, carry sunscreen, and bring a warm layer as summit temperatures can drop significantly even in November. Start no later than 8:00 AM to avoid afternoon cloud cover on the summit. The Tiki Trail is free to access — no gondola ticket needed.

day_by_day.morning: Active recovery morning — take a gentle walk along the Queenstown Gardens loop track (free, ~1 hour, flat terrain). Explore the rose gardens, frisbee golf course, and lakeside paths. Great spot for photography and relaxing after the big hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Queenstown i-SITE visitor centre to book or confirm the Routeburn Track Day Hike and any bungee jumping experiences. Then head to Arthurs Point to scout the Shotover River canyon area. Walk the short Gorge Road track for free river views. Alternatively, visit the free Kiwi Birdlife Park surrounds or walk up to the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (2–3 hours, free, great views).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Queenstown Night Market on Earl Street (Thursday–Sunday) or cook a simple meal at the accommodation. If the night market is running, enjoy diverse street food from $5–12 NZD per dish.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — cereal, toast, or eggs bought from Countdown supermarket
meals.lunch: The Cow restaurant on Cow Lane for budget pizza slices or a cheap wrap from Subway on the main street (~$10–14 NZD)
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market street food (if open) or self-catered pasta dinner at accommodation to save money

day_by_day.notes: Use this day strategically to plan and book upcoming activities. Bungee jumping with AJ Hackett (Kawarau Bridge) can be booked online in advance for better rates — look for early-bird or online discounts. Check weather forecasts for the Routeburn Track hike day.

day_by_day.morning: Bungee jumping day! Head to the AJ Hackett Kawarau Bridge Bungy — the world's first commercial bungee site, located 23km from Queenstown (take the Nomad Safaris shuttle or join a shared transfer, ~$10–15 NZD each way). Watch other jumpers from the free viewing platform first to build courage. Then take the plunge from the 43m Kawarau Bridge over the turquoise river.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown and celebrate your jump. Walk along the lakefront and visit the free Underwater Observatory at the end of Queenstown Pier (small fee ~$20 NZD) or simply relax by the lake. Alternatively, take a free walk up to the Bob's Peak viewpoint via the Tiki Trail for a different perspective of the town.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner to celebrate the bungee jump milestone. Explore Queenstown's restaurant strip along Beach Street and Shotover Street.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at accommodation before heading out
meals.lunch: Grab a meat pie or sandwich from a petrol station or bakery near Kawarau Bridge (~$5–8 NZD) — keep it light before jumping
meals.dinner: Rata restaurant for a splurge-worthy local meal (budget ~$30–40 NZD) or Fishbone Bar & Grill for fresh fish and chips (~$20–25 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: AJ Hackett Kawarau Bridge Bungy costs approximately $175–200 NZD per person — book online in advance for the best price and to secure your preferred time slot. Arrive early as the site gets busy. You can add a video/photo package but this adds cost — weigh up whether it fits your budget. Wear comfortable, secure clothing and remove loose items.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Glenorchy — take the Orbus Route 5 or join a cheap shared shuttle (~$15–20 NZD return) along the stunning Lake Wakatipu shoreline road (45 minutes each way). Arrive in the small, picturesque village of Glenorchy, gateway to the Routeburn and Greenstone tracks. Walk the free Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway (1.5 hours, flat, beautiful birdlife and mountain reflections).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Glenorchy with a free walk to the Glenorchy Wharf for incredible views of Mount Earnslaw and the Dart River flats. Have a picnic lunch by the lake. Begin the return journey to Queenstown in the mid-afternoon, stopping at any scenic pull-offs along the lake road for photos.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Queenstown, visit the Queenstown Night Market on Earl Street (Thursday evenings) for affordable street food from around the world. Enjoy the live music and relaxed atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation before departure
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch by the Glenorchy Wharf — supplies from Queenstown supermarket the night before
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market on Earl Street — budget $10–20 NZD for a full meal from the food stalls

day_by_day.notes: The Queenstown to Glenorchy road is considered one of the most scenic drives in New Zealand — sit on the left side of the shuttle for the best lake views. Glenorchy has very limited facilities so bring all food and water from Queenstown. This is also a great opportunity to scout the start of the Routeburn Track trailhead if you want to see it ahead of your hike day.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Day Hike — one of New Zealand's Great Walks. Take the early shuttle from Queenstown to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead near Glenorchy (book in advance, ~$30–40 NZD return with Trackhopper or similar shuttle service). Begin hiking through ancient beech forests alongside the Routeburn River. The track to Routeburn Flats Hut takes approximately 2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue beyond Routeburn Flats Hut toward Routeburn Falls Hut (another 1.5–2 hours, climbing steeply). Enjoy spectacular alpine scenery, waterfalls, and views of the Darran Mountains. Eat lunch at Routeburn Falls Hut with panoramic views. Begin the return hike back to the trailhead (allow 3–3.5 hours for the descent). Meet the return shuttle at the agreed pick-up time.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown tired but exhilarated. A gentle walk along the lakefront to stretch legs. Early dinner and an early night to recover.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at accommodation — eat well before the big hike
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Routeburn Falls Hut — sandwiches, energy bars, fruit, and snacks prepared the night before
meals.dinner: Burger culture on Beach Street for a satisfying post-hike burger (~$15–20 NZD) or self-catered noodles at accommodation

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track day hike to Routeburn Falls and back is approximately 16km return and rated moderate-to-hard. Start early (shuttle departs ~7:30–8:00 AM). Carry plenty of water, sunscreen, a rain jacket, and warm layers — alpine weather can change rapidly even in November. No Great Walk pass is required for a day hike. Book the shuttle well in advance as spaces fill quickly in summer.

day_by_day.morning: Well-deserved rest morning after two big hikes. Sleep in, do laundry, and reorganise your pack. Visit the Queenstown Farmers Market at Earnslaw Park (Saturday mornings, 9:00 AM–1:00 PM) for fresh local produce, artisan food, and cheap breakfast bites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the free Queenstown Hill Time Walk (2–3 hours return, moderate difficulty) for a different vantage point of the lake and town. The summit features a 'Basket of Dreams' sculpture. Alternatively, rent a bike from Outside Sports (~$30–40 NZD for half a day) and cycle the Queenstown Trail along the lake edge toward Frankton.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Skyline Gondola viewing area — instead of paying for the gondola (~$35 NZD), hike up the free Tiki Trail to Bob's Peak for sunset views over Queenstown and Lake Wakatipu. A magical way to spend a free evening.

meals.breakfast: Queenstown Farmers Market — grab fresh pastries, coffee, and fruit for ~$10–15 NZD
meals.lunch: Self-catered at accommodation using farmers market produce
meals.dinner: The Cow restaurant on Cow Lane — famous for cheap, hearty pizza and pasta in a cosy rustic setting (~$18–25 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is a great day to restock supplies at the Countdown supermarket on Gorge Road for the week ahead. The Queenstown Farmers Market is a highlight — arrive by 9:30 AM for the best selection. If you plan to do the Nevis Bungy or any other adventure activity later in the trip, today is a good day to book it.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Arrowtown — take the Orbus Route 8 from Queenstown (~$2–4 NZD, 25 minutes). Explore this beautifully preserved 1860s gold rush town with its tree-lined main street, heritage stone buildings, and boutique shops. Visit the free Lakes District Museum to learn about the region's gold mining and Māori history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the free Arrow River Gorge Walk from Arrowtown (2–3 hours return, easy-moderate) following the Arrow River through a dramatic schist gorge. Try gold panning in the river (free activity — bring a pan or use a stick). Return to Arrowtown for afternoon tea before catching the bus back to Queenstown.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening in Queenstown. Visit the lakefront for the sunset, then grab takeaways and eat by the water.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation before departure
meals.lunch: Arrowtown's Provisions café for affordable sandwiches and coffee (~$12–18 NZD) or a packed lunch from Queenstown
meals.dinner: Takeaway fish and chips from Queenstown Fish & Chippery near the waterfront (~$12–15 NZD) — eat by the lake

day_by_day.notes: Arrowtown is one of the most charming towns in New Zealand and entry to most attractions is free. Autumn colours in Arrowtown are legendary but November brings lush green foliage instead — still very scenic. The Arrow River Gorge Walk is an underrated gem and completely free. Wear sturdy shoes as the riverbank track can be uneven.

day_by_day.morning: Adventure day — Nevis Bungy or Ledge Bungy option. The Ledge Bungy at the top of the Skyline Gondola is more budget-friendly (~$165 NZD) and offers a unique urban bungee experience above Queenstown at night or day. Alternatively, if budget allows, the Nevis Bungy (~$275 NZD) is New Zealand's highest bungy at 134m — a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Book whichever fits your budget.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the jump, take the gondola back down (included in Ledge Bungy price) and spend the afternoon exploring the Queenstown Gardens in detail — lawn bowls, frisbee golf, and lakeside paths. All free. Alternatively, walk the One Mile Creek Track (free, 1.5 hours) through native bush behind the town.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Kiwi Birdlife Park for the free 4:00 PM or 5:00 PM conservation show (entry to the show is free; full park entry ~$49 NZD — decide based on budget). Enjoy dinner at a local favourite.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — eat well before the bungy
meals.lunch: World Bar on Church Street for cheap bar snacks and teapot cocktails (~$10–15 NZD for food)
meals.dinner: Winnies Gourmet Pizza Bar on The Mall for affordable wood-fired pizza (~$20–28 NZD) — a Queenstown local favourite

day_by_day.notes: If you already did the Kawarau Bridge Bungy on Day 4, consider whether a second bungy fits your budget. The Ledge Bungy is the most affordable AJ Hackett option in Queenstown. Alternatively, replace this with a free hiking day on the Queenstown Hill or a bike ride along the Queenstown Trail to save money for other experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Wanaka — take the Ritchies InterIslander bus or Atomic Travel coach from Queenstown to Wanaka (~$20–25 NZD one way, 1 hour via the Crown Range or 1.5 hours via Cromwell). Arrive in Wanaka and walk the free Wanaka Lakefront Promenade. Visit the famous 'That Wanaka Tree' — a lone willow tree growing in the lake, one of New Zealand's most photographed spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the free Diamond Lake and Rocky Mountain Loop Track near Wanaka (3–4 hours, moderate difficulty, stunning views over Lake Wanaka and Mount Aspiring National Park). Alternatively, walk the free Roys Peak Track for 2–3 hours if you have the energy (full summit takes 5–6 hours). Return to Wanaka town for a late afternoon wander.
day_by_day.evening: Return bus to Queenstown in the early evening. Grab a cheap dinner on arrival back in town.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation before departing for Wanaka
meals.lunch: Wanaka's Francesca's Italian Kitchen for affordable pasta (~$18–22 NZD) or a packed lunch eaten at Diamond Lake
meals.dinner: Self-catered at accommodation on return to Queenstown to save money after a full travel day

day_by_day.notes: Book the bus to Wanaka in advance as seats fill up, especially in summer. The Crown Range Road (via Cardrona) is the highest sealed road in New Zealand and offers breathtaking views — try to sit on the right side of the bus going to Wanaka. Wanaka is a beautiful, slightly quieter alternative to Queenstown and well worth the day trip. Confirm return bus times before leaving Queenstown.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Queenstown Bike Trail — rent a bike from Vertigo Bikes or Outside Sports (~$30–50 NZD for a full day) and ride the Queenstown Trail along the shores of Lake Wakatipu toward Kelvin Heights Peninsula. The flat lakeside trail offers incredible mountain scenery with minimal effort. Ride to Kelvin Heights and back (~20km return, 2–3 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return bikes and spend the afternoon at the Queenstown Beach by the lakefront. Swim in Lake Wakatipu (free — the water is cold but refreshing in November). Alternatively, walk the free Fernhill Loop Track through native bush above the town (2–3 hours, moderate). Great views over the Remarkables.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a slightly nicer restaurant as the trip winds down. Explore Queenstown's vibrant bar scene on Shotover Street for a drink or two at budget-friendly bars.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation
meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich and cold drink from a petrol station or New World supermarket along the bike trail near Frankton (~$8–12 NZD)
meals.dinner: Bao Now on Camp Street for affordable Asian-fusion bao buns (~$15–20 NZD) or Habebe's on Shotover Street for cheap Middle Eastern wraps

day_by_day.notes: The Queenstown Trail is a well-maintained multi-use path suitable for all fitness levels. The section to Kelvin Heights is particularly scenic and flat. If you prefer not to rent bikes, this section is also walkable (allow 4–5 hours return on foot). Check bike rental opening times as some shops open late.

day_by_day.morning: Final full hiking day — tackle the Queenstown Hill Time Walk if you haven't done it yet, or revisit a favourite trail. Alternatively, take a free walk along the Sunshine Bay Track from Queenstown Gardens to Sunshine Bay (2 hours return, easy, beautiful lake views). A peaceful way to spend a final morning in nature.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to town and spend the afternoon doing any last-minute souvenir shopping on Beach Street and Camp Street. Visit the Queenstown i-SITE for any free maps or brochures to take home. Pack your bags and prepare for departure. Do a final supermarket run to use up any remaining New Zealand dollars on snacks for the journey home.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Queenstown — return to a favourite restaurant or try somewhere new. Enjoy a last walk along the illuminated Queenstown lakefront at night, watching the lights reflect on Lake Wakatipu.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — use up remaining food supplies
meals.lunch: Fergburger for a final iconic Queenstown burger (~$15–20 NZD) — the perfect farewell lunch
meals.dinner: Self-catered at accommodation to save money, or a final cheap eat at the Night Market if it's running (Thursday evenings on Earl Street)

day_by_day.notes: Check out time from Queenstown Boutique Stay — confirm with the property whether you can store luggage if your flight is the following day. Spend any remaining NZD cash as it can be difficult to exchange small amounts abroad. Back up all your photos and videos from the trip. Reflect on an incredible 12 days in one of the world's most stunning destinations.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown — check out of Queenstown Boutique Stay. If time allows before departure, take one last walk along the Queenstown lakefront or grab a coffee at a local café. Head to Queenstown Airport via Orbus Route 1 (~$2–4 NZD) or arrange a shuttle transfer (~$15–20 NZD shared). Allow at least 90 minutes before your flight for check-in and security.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Queenstown Airport. Reflect on an incredible 13-day adventure through the South Island — two world-class hikes, multiple bungee jumps, and countless free scenic experiences across one of the most breathtaking regions on Earth.
day_by_day.evening: In transit — enjoy the aerial views of the Southern Alps, Lake Wakatipu, and Fiordland as the plane climbs out of Queenstown. A fitting farewell to New Zealand's South Island.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast at accommodation before check-out, or grab a coffee and pastry from a café near the hotel
meals.lunch: Airport café or bring packed snacks to avoid expensive airport food prices
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport food depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Queenstown Airport is small — allow plenty of time for check-in, especially if you have checked luggage or sports equipment. Orbus Route 1 runs regularly to the airport from the town centre. Confirm your flight details and any departure taxes. Ensure all adventure activity receipts and travel insurance documents are safely stored. New Zealand requires all visitors to pay a $35 NZD International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL) — this is typically included in your flight booking.

trip_options.title: Classic New Zealand South Island Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight LH lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Land at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage, clear customs, and transfer to Queenstown Boutique Stay (~15 min). Check in, freshen up, then take a leisurely stroll along Queenstown Bay waterfront and explore the town centre to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the lively Queenstown CBD, browse the shops on Beach Street, and enjoy the lakefront views as the sun sets over the Remarkables mountain range.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a nearby café upon arrival — try Vudu Café on Rees Street for a sandwich and flat white (~NZD 18–22)
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant on The Mall — a celebrated Queenstown dining institution with seasonal New Zealand produce. Mid-range mains NZD 35–50. Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag may be a factor. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance in case your room isn't ready at 13:00. Pick up a local SIM card at the airport if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Ben Lomond Summit Hike — Start early (7:30am) from the Queenstown Gondola base. Take the gondola up to Skyline (optional, ~NZD 40) then hike the Ben Lomond Track. The summit sits at 1,748m with 360-degree panoramic views over Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables. Allow 6–8 hours total.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Ben Lomond descent, arriving back in town mid-to-late afternoon. Rest your legs and grab a coffee at a lakefront café. Visit the Queenstown Gardens for a gentle cool-down walk.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and recover. Enjoy a quiet dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or grab a muffin and coffee from Vudu Café before hitting the trail
meals.lunch: Pack your own trail lunch — pick up supplies the evening before from a Queenstown supermarket (Countdown on Gorge Road). Sandwiches, trail mix, energy bars.
meals.dinner: Fergburger on Shot Over Street — Queenstown's legendary burger joint, iconic and affordable. Expect a queue. Budget NZD 15–22.

day_by_day.notes: This is a strenuous full-day hike. Wear layers — summit temperatures can be 10–15°C cooler than the town. Bring plenty of water (2L+), sunscreen, and a rain jacket. Check weather forecast the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Kawarau Bridge Bungee Jump — Head out to the world's first commercial bungee jump site, 23km from Queenstown (~25 min drive). Jump from the iconic 43m Kawarau Bridge above the turquoise river gorge. Watch others jump before your turn. Allow 2–3 hours including travel and the experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown. Visit the Kiwi Birdlife Park near the gondola base for a relaxed afternoon — see kiwi birds, conservation shows, and native bush walks. Entry ~NZD 55.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's bar scene on The Mall or Cow Lane for a celebratory post-bungee drink.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hotel or a café — try The Bespoke Kitchen on Isle Street for healthy bowls and eggs (~NZD 18–25)
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Kawarau Bungy Centre café on-site, or pack a light lunch. Budget ~NZD 15–20.
meals.dinner: Pub-style dinner at Winnies on The Mall — great pizzas and a lively atmosphere. Budget NZD 25–35.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kawarau Bungee Jump in advance through AJ Hackett Bungy (bungyjump.com). Cost is approximately NZD 250. Wear comfortable, secure clothing. Tandem jumps are available if travelling with a partner.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy — New Zealand's highest bungee jump at 134m above the Nevis River gorge. Transfer from Queenstown CBD via AJ Hackett shuttle (~45 min). The pod is suspended by cables above the gorge — an adrenaline experience unlike any other. Allow half a day including transport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown by early afternoon. Recover with a scenic cruise on Lake Wakatipu — the TSS Earnslaw vintage steamship departs from the Queenstown Pier. A 1-hour cruise costs ~NZD 65 and offers stunning views of the surrounding mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Lakefront dinner with a relaxed atmosphere to wind down after two big bungee days.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick grab-and-go from a bakery — you'll need to be at the AJ Hackett booking centre early
meals.lunch: Light lunch back in town after returning — try Yonder on Beach Street for casual bites (~NZD 18–28)
meals.dinner: Botswana Butchery on Marine Parade — elegant lakefront dining with excellent New Zealand beef and lamb. Mains NZD 40–55.

day_by_day.notes: Nevis Bungy costs approximately NZD 350. Book well in advance as it fills up fast, especially in peak November season. Weight and health restrictions apply — check AJ Hackett's website. The shuttle departs from the Queenstown booking centre.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Day Hike — Depart Queenstown early (~7:00am) for the 1.5-hour drive to the Routeburn Track trailhead. This world-renowned Great Walk offers stunning alpine scenery, beech forests, and views of the Darran Mountains. Hike to Routeburn Falls Hut and back, or continue to Lake Harris if fitness allows. Allow 6–8 hours on the trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking or begin the return journey to Queenstown, arriving back in the late afternoon. The drive back through the Wakatipu Basin is scenic and rewarding.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and a quiet dinner — your legs will thank you for an early night.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or grab a packed breakfast the night before from a supermarket
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch — prepare the night before. Sandwiches, fruit, nuts, chocolate.
meals.dinner: Pub dinner at The World Bar on Church Street — relaxed, affordable, great cocktails. Budget NZD 20–30.

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track trailhead is accessed via Glenorchy Road — one of New Zealand's most scenic drives. Consider taking the Glenorchy-Queenstown shuttle if you prefer not to drive. No booking required for a day hike but carry the DOC intentions card. Weather in the alpine zone can change rapidly.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — sleep in and enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Spend the morning exploring Queenstown's arts and craft scene, visiting the Queenstown Arts Centre or browsing boutique shops on Camp Street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a jet boat ride on the Shotover River — the Shotover Jet is a thrilling 25-minute ride through narrow canyons just 10 minutes from town (~NZD 159). A great lower-intensity adrenaline activity after the big hikes and jumps.
day_by_day.evening: Head up to Skyline Queenstown via the gondola for sunset views and dinner at the Stratosfare Restaurant. The gondola costs ~NZD 40 return.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast or brunch at Vudu Café — eggs benedict and a long black (~NZD 22–28)
meals.lunch: Light lunch in town — try Habebe on Beach Street for Middle Eastern wraps and bowls (~NZD 15–20)
meals.dinner: Stratosfare Restaurant at Skyline — buffet-style with panoramic views over Queenstown and the lake. Budget NZD 65–80 including gondola.

day_by_day.notes: A well-earned rest day with lighter activities. November evenings in Queenstown are long (sunset around 9:00pm) so the gondola views are spectacular. Book the gondola and Stratosfare dinner in advance online.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Milford Sound — Depart Queenstown at 6:00am for the 4-hour scenic drive through Te Anau and Fiordland National Park. The drive itself is breathtaking, passing through ancient beech forests and alongside glacial lakes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Milford Sound for a 2-hour scenic cruise through the fiord, passing Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls, and Bowen Falls. Seals, dolphins, and penguins are commonly spotted. Cruise departs around 1:00–2:00pm (~NZD 85–120).
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return drive to Queenstown, arriving back around 9:00–10:00pm. This is a long day — pack snacks and podcasts for the drive.

meals.breakfast: Very early — grab coffee and a pastry from a 24-hour petrol station or pack from the hotel the night before
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Milford Sound Lodge café or the Milford Sound visitor centre café. Budget NZD 20–30.
meals.dinner: Late dinner at a Queenstown takeaway — Fergburger is open late, or grab pizza from Hell Pizza. Budget NZD 15–25.

day_by_day.notes: This is a long but iconic day trip (~10–11 hours total). Consider booking a guided day tour from Queenstown which handles transport and the cruise — companies like RealNZ offer full-day packages from ~NZD 250. Alternatively, drive yourself and book the cruise separately. Sandflies at Milford Sound are fierce — bring insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Glenorchy day trip — Drive the stunning 45km Glenorchy Road along Lake Wakatipu's western shore to the small village of Glenorchy (45 min). Walk the Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway (~1.5 hours, easy) through wetlands with mountain reflections. This area was used as a filming location for Lord of the Rings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Paradise area beyond Glenorchy (4WD or standard vehicle on Paradise Road). Short walks around the iconic cotton grass flats and beech forest. Return to Queenstown by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Queenstown. Visit the Saturday night markets or explore the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing for Glenorchy
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Glenorchy Café — a beloved local institution with great pies, sandwiches, and coffee. Budget NZD 15–20.
meals.dinner: Fishbone Bar & Grill on Beach Street — excellent New Zealand seafood in a relaxed setting. Mains NZD 30–45.

day_by_day.notes: The Glenorchy Road is widely regarded as one of the world's most scenic drives. Depart early for the best light on the lake. The Paradise area may require a high-clearance vehicle depending on recent weather — check road conditions locally.

day_by_day.morning: Wanaka day trip — Drive to Wanaka (~1 hour via the Crown Range Road, New Zealand's highest sealed road). Stop at the Crown Range summit lookout for panoramic views. Arrive in Wanaka and visit the famous 'Wanaka Tree' (lone willow in the lake) for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Roys Peak Track from Wanaka township — a popular 16km return hike with famous views of Lake Wanaka and Mount Aspiring. Allow 5–6 hours, or hike partway (2–3 hours) to the first viewpoints and return. Alternatively, explore Wanaka township and visit Puzzling World (~NZD 22).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown via the Crown Range Road at sunset for dramatic golden-hour views.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or grab coffee on the Crown Range drive
meals.lunch: Lunch in Wanaka — try Francesca's Italian Kitchen on Helwick Street for pasta and pizza (~NZD 25–35)
meals.dinner: Back in Queenstown — Bao Now on The Mall for Asian-inspired bao buns and noodles. Budget NZD 20–30.

day_by_day.notes: Roys Peak Track is closed from October 1 to November 10 for lambing season — by November 23 it should be open, but confirm with the DOC website before visiting. The Crown Range Road is steep and winding — drive carefully, especially in the evening. Carry water and layers for the hike.

day_by_day.morning: Te Anau and Fiordland day trip — Drive to Te Anau (~2 hours) and visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves. A guided boat tour takes you through underground caverns lit by thousands of glowworms. Tours run throughout the day, ~NZD 100. Book in advance through RealNZ.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Te Anau township and walk the Te Anau lakefront. Visit the DOC Te Anau visitor centre to learn about Fiordland's ecology. Optional: short walk on the Kepler Track from the Te Anau boat ramp (easy 1–2 hour section through beech forest).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown (~2 hours). Dinner and early night.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing
meals.lunch: Lunch in Te Anau — The Fat Duck Café on Town Centre is popular and affordable. Budget NZD 18–25.
meals.dinner: The Cow Restaurant on Cow Lane, Queenstown — cosy stone-walled restaurant famous for fondue and pizza. Budget NZD 30–40.

day_by_day.notes: The glowworm caves tour lasts approximately 2 hours. Photography inside the caves is not permitted. Dress warmly as the caves are cool (~12°C). The Kepler Track section near Te Anau is flat and easy — suitable for tired legs.

day_by_day.morning: Arrowtown visit — Drive 20 minutes from Queenstown to the charming historic gold-mining town of Arrowtown. Walk the Arrow River Gorge trail (easy, 1–2 hours) along the river where gold was discovered in the 1860s. Try gold panning at the river's edge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Arrowtown's heritage buildings, boutique shops, and galleries on Buckingham Street. Visit the Lakes District Museum & Gallery (~NZD 10). Drive back to Queenstown and spend the afternoon at leisure — spa, shopping, or relaxing at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Final big evening out in Queenstown — celebrate the trip with a special dinner.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch in Arrowtown — Provisions of Arrowtown on Buckingham Street is a beloved local café with excellent food. Budget NZD 20–28.
meals.dinner: Amisfield Winery & Bistro near Arrowtown (or return for dinner) — one of Central Otago's finest dining experiences in a vineyard setting. Mains NZD 40–60. Book well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Arrowtown is at peak autumn beauty in April–May, but November brings lush greenery and wildflowers. The Arrow River Gorge walk can be extended to a full half-day if desired. Amisfield is a 15-minute drive from Queenstown — consider booking a taxi/rideshare for dinner if you plan to enjoy Central Otago wines.

day_by_day.morning: Half-day mountain biking on the Queenstown Bike Park — accessed via the Skyline gondola, this world-class bike park has trails for all levels. Rent a bike at the base (~NZD 80–120 including gondola). Alternatively, take a guided e-bike tour through the Queenstown trails for a more relaxed option.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel and pack for departure. Final walk along the Queenstown waterfront — visit the Queenstown Bay beach, grab an ice cream, and soak in the last views of the Remarkables and Cecil Peak across the lake.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a favourite spot from the trip, or try something new. Spend the evening reflecting on the journey.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — make the most of it on the second-to-last day
meals.lunch: Post-biking refuel at Skyline's café or back in town at Vudu Café — a full circle moment from Day 1. Budget NZD 18–25.
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant (revisit) or try Queenstown's Sherwood Hotel restaurant for farm-to-table New Zealand cuisine. Mains NZD 35–50.

day_by_day.notes: If mountain biking feels too strenuous after 12 days of activity, swap for a relaxed kayak on Lake Wakatipu (rental ~NZD 30/hour) or a final visit to the Queenstown Gardens. Confirm any remaining hotel bills and arrange airport transfer for the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown — wake up early for one last sunrise walk to the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (2–3 hours return, easy-moderate) for sweeping views over the town and lake in the morning light. Alternatively, enjoy a slow hotel breakfast and pack at leisure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from Queenstown Boutique Stay. Transfer to Queenstown Airport for your departure flight. Allow 1.5–2 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Pick up last-minute New Zealand souvenirs at the airport — Whittaker's chocolate, Manuka honey, and Merino wool goods are excellent options.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — farewell New Zealand!

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a last coffee and pastry at Vudu Café on the way to the hill walk
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a quick café stop before heading to the terminal. Budget NZD 15–20.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at your transit airport

day_by_day.notes: Queenstown Airport is small but busy — arrive early, especially in peak November season. Confirm flight details and check-in requirements the night before. The Queenstown Hill Time Walk is a lovely, quiet farewell to the South Island — start by 6:30am for the best morning light and to be back in time for checkout.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
experiences.description: One of New Zealand's most iconic day hikes, this 19.4km trek crosses an active volcanic landscape with emerald lakes, steaming vents, and panoramic views. Book a shuttle from Queenstown or Wanaka for an early morning start. Since your flight arrives late on Day 1, plan this for Day 2 or later when you are well-rested and settled near the trailhead.
experiences.location: Tongariro National Park, Central South Island

experiences.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungee Jump
experiences.description: The world's first commercial bungee jump site, located just 23km from Queenstown CBD. At 43 metres above the Kawarau River, this is the perfect introduction to bungee jumping. Stay in central Queenstown to be within easy reach of this iconic activity and avoid long transfers after your late arrival on Day 1.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy - New Zealand's Highest Bungee
experiences.description: A 134-metre freefall suspended above the Nevis River gorge, this is New Zealand's highest bungee jump and one of the most thrilling in the world. A dedicated bus departs from Queenstown town centre, making it easy to access if you are staying centrally. Schedule this mid-trip when you are fully acclimatised.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Day Hike
experiences.description: A world-renowned Great Walk offering stunning alpine scenery, beech forests, and views of the Darran Mountains. The day hike to Routeburn Falls and Lake Harris is achievable without a multi-day permit. Stay in Glenorchy or central Queenstown to minimise travel time to the trailhead and make the most of daylight hours.

experiences.name: Ben Lomond Summit Hike
experiences.description: A challenging full-day hike rising 1748 metres above sea level with sweeping 360-degree views over Queenstown, Lake Wakatipu, and the Remarkables. The trailhead is accessible directly from Queenstown town centre via the Skyline gondola or on foot, making it ideal if you are staying centrally. A perfect activity from Day 2 onwards once you have recovered from your late arrival.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Private transfer to Queenstown Boutique Stay. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the Queenstown waterfront promenade to get oriented with the town and enjoy views of Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables mountain range.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on Lake Wakatipu aboard a private charter, followed by a relaxed first evening in town exploring the vibrant Queenstown dining scene.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or onboard — N/A
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant by Josh Emmett — one of Queenstown's finest, offering contemporary New Zealand cuisine with locally sourced ingredients in an elegant setting on The Mall.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings at the hotel concierge desk this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Kawarau Bridge Bungee Jump — head to the world's first commercial bungee site, just 23km from Queenstown CBD. At 43 metres above the turquoise Kawarau River, this iconic leap is a thrilling and historic way to kick off your adventure. Book the VIP experience for private jump slots and professional photography/video package.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown and take the Skyline Gondola up Bob's Peak for panoramic views over the lake and town. Enjoy a leisurely walk along the ridge trails at the top before descending.
day_by_day.evening: Relax with a wine tasting at a lakeside bar, then enjoy a premium dinner overlooking the water.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at Queenstown Boutique Stay — fuel up well before the jump.
meals.lunch: The Bunker Restaurant — a cosy, intimate Queenstown institution known for its excellent bistro menu and curated wine list, perfect post-jump.
meals.dinner: Amisfield Winery & Bistro — a short drive from Queenstown, offering a legendary 'Trust the Chef' degustation menu paired with their celebrated Central Otago wines in a stunning vineyard setting.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Kawarau Bridge early to secure your preferred jump time. Wear comfortable, layered clothing. Book Amisfield well in advance as it fills quickly. Private driver recommended for the winery dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy — New Zealand's highest bungee jump at 134 metres above the Nevis River gorge. Transfer via 4WD to the remote canyon location. The suspended pod and breathtaking freefall make this a world-class adrenaline experience. Book the premium package including HD video, photos, and a personalised certificate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Recovery and rejuvenation — return to Queenstown and treat yourself to a luxury spa session at a premium day spa. The ONSEN Hot Pools perched above the Shotover River offer private thermal pools with stunning gorge views, perfect for post-jump muscle recovery.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening in Queenstown town centre, browsing the boutique shops and enjoying the lively atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — high-protein meal recommended before the jump.
meals.lunch: Vudu Cafe & Larder — a beloved Queenstown favourite known for wholesome, beautifully crafted meals using local produce, ideal for a relaxed post-Nevis lunch.
meals.dinner: Flame Bar & Grill — premium steakhouse experience featuring New Zealand grass-fed beef and Central Otago wines with stunning lake views.

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy requires a 4WD transfer from Queenstown — allow 45 minutes each way. Minimum weight requirements apply. Book ONSEN Hot Pools in advance as private pools sell out quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Ben Lomond Summit Hike — an early start for this challenging full-day alpine hike rising to 1,748 metres above sea level. Take the Skyline Gondola to Bob's Peak to save elevation, then follow the well-marked trail through tussock and alpine terrain to the summit for sweeping 360-degree views of Queenstown, Lake Wakatipu, and the surrounding ranges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the descent back to the gondola base or hike all the way down to town. The full return hike takes approximately 7–9 hours, so the afternoon will be spent completing the descent and recovering.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner after conquering Ben Lomond.

meals.breakfast: Early in-hotel breakfast — pack a premium trail lunch prepared by the hotel kitchen.
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet trail lunch provided by the hotel — enjoy at the summit with panoramic views.
meals.dinner: Botswana Butchery — a Queenstown institution on the lakefront offering exceptional dry-aged cuts, fresh seafood, and an outstanding wine list in a sophisticated atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Start hiking by 7:30am to allow ample time. Wear sturdy hiking boots and carry layers — summit weather can change rapidly in November. Apply sunscreen generously. The gondola operates from early morning and saves approximately 400m of elevation gain.

day_by_day.morning: Active rest day — gentle morning walk along the Queenstown Gardens lakeside loop (approximately 3km, flat and scenic). Visit the rose garden and enjoy the peaceful surroundings before a late breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jet boat experience on the Shotover River — the Shotover Jet is one of New Zealand's most exhilarating jet boat rides, blasting through narrow rock canyons at high speed. Book the premium private charter option for a more exclusive experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar followed by a fine dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Late breakfast at Vudu Larder & Bakery — indulge in their famous pastries, eggs, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Provisions of Queenstown — a charming deli and café offering artisan sandwiches, charcuterie boards, and excellent coffee, perfect for a light pre-jet boat lunch.
meals.dinner: Pier 19 — a sophisticated waterfront restaurant offering premium seafood, including locally caught fish and Bluff oysters, with spectacular lake and mountain views.

day_by_day.notes: Day 5 is intentionally lighter to allow recovery after consecutive high-intensity days. The Shotover Jet departs from Arthur's Point, a short drive from Queenstown. Book in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Day Hike — depart early for one of New Zealand's most celebrated Great Walks. A private guided day hike option is highly recommended for a premium experience. The trail winds through ancient beech forests, past alpine lakes, and offers dramatic views of the Darran Mountains and Hollyford Valley. Hike to the Routeburn Falls Hut and beyond toward Lake Harris if fitness allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the upper sections of the Routeburn Track before returning to the trailhead in the late afternoon. The return journey to Queenstown takes approximately 1.5 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Queenstown after a big hiking day.

meals.breakfast: Early in-hotel breakfast — depart by 7:00am to maximise time on the track.
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the hotel — enjoy at Routeburn Falls with waterfall views.
meals.dinner: The Stonewall Restaurant — intimate fine dining in a heritage stone building, featuring seasonal tasting menus with New Zealand lamb, venison, and fresh seafood.

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track trailhead is approximately 75km from Queenstown (about 1.5 hours). A private guided experience enhances the hike significantly — guides provide ecological and geological context. Book transport and guide well in advance. November weather is generally good but carry rain gear.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic helicopter flight over Fiordland and Milford Sound — depart Queenstown on a premium helicopter tour flying over the Southern Alps, Fiordland National Park, and Milford Sound. Many operators offer a glacier or remote alpine landing as part of the experience. This is one of the most spectacular ways to appreciate the scale of the South Island landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown by early afternoon. Spend the afternoon at leisure — visit the Queenstown Arts Centre or browse the boutique galleries and luxury stores along The Mall.
day_by_day.evening: Premium wine and cheese experience at a local cellar door or wine bar.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — depart for helicopter by 9:00am.
meals.lunch: Rata Restaurant — return for lunch this time, enjoying their acclaimed seasonal menu in a more relaxed daytime atmosphere.
meals.dinner: Kō Restaurant at The Rees Hotel — a lakefront fine dining experience celebrating Māori culinary traditions and New Zealand kai (food) in a contemporary luxury setting.

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter flights are weather-dependent — the operator will confirm on the morning of the flight. November is generally excellent for flying. Book the premium Milford Sound helicopter experience months in advance as it is extremely popular.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Arrowtown — a beautifully preserved gold rush village 20 minutes from Queenstown. Explore the historic Chinese settlement, the Lakes District Museum, and the charming main street lined with heritage buildings and boutique shops. Walk the Arrow River Bridges Track (approximately 2 hours return) through stunning autumn-tinged willows along the river gorge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Gibbston Valley — the heart of Central Otago wine country. Tour the famous Gibbston Valley Winery cave cellar, sample their award-winning Pinot Noir, and explore the surrounding vineyard landscape. Book a private winery tour for a premium experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown for a relaxed final evening in the area.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast before departing for Arrowtown.
meals.lunch: The Chop Shop Food Merchants, Arrowtown — a beloved local favourite serving excellent burgers, salads, and craft beverages in a relaxed setting.
meals.dinner: Amisfield Winery & Bistro (second visit for the full degustation experience if not done on Day 2, or alternatively) Madam Woo — a vibrant Malaysian-inspired restaurant on The Mall offering beautifully crafted Southeast Asian dishes and a lively atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Arrowtown and Gibbston Valley can be combined in a single day trip comfortably. A private driver or rental car is recommended. Gibbston Valley cave tours must be pre-booked.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer to Te Anau — depart Queenstown after breakfast for the 2.5-hour scenic drive to Te Anau, the gateway to Fiordland. The drive passes through Kingston, along Lake Wakatipu, and through rolling farmland and native bush. Check in to a premium Te Anau lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Te Anau Glowworm Caves — take a boat across Lake Te Anau to explore the magical glowworm caves hidden within the lake's western shore. A guided tour leads you through dramatic limestone formations and a silent underground boat ride beneath thousands of glowworms. Book the premium evening tour for a more intimate experience.
day_by_day.evening: Lakeside dinner in Te Anau with views over the glassy lake toward the Fiordland mountains.

meals.breakfast: Final in-hotel breakfast at Queenstown Boutique Stay.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the car during the scenic drive — arrange with the hotel the night before.
meals.dinner: Redcliff Café & Bar, Te Anau — a charming heritage cottage restaurant offering excellent New Zealand game, venison, and fresh fish with a warm, intimate atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: The Te Anau Glowworm Caves tour is operated by Real Journeys and must be booked in advance. The evening tour is smaller and more atmospheric. Accommodation in Te Anau: consider Fiordland Lodge for a premium lakeside experience.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Sound full-day experience — depart Te Anau early for the iconic 2-hour drive through Fiordland National Park to Milford Sound, passing through the Homer Tunnel and some of New Zealand's most dramatic mountain scenery. Stop at The Chasm and Mirror Lakes along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium Milford Sound cruise — board a luxury small-group vessel for a scenic cruise through the fiord, passing Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls, Bowen Falls, and abundant wildlife including fur seals, dolphins, and penguins. Opt for an overnight cruise vessel or a kayaking experience within the fiord for an immersive premium encounter.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Te Anau by early evening. Quiet dinner and early rest.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Te Anau lodge — depart by 7:30am.
meals.lunch: Onboard the Milford Sound cruise — premium vessels offer excellent buffet lunches with local produce and New Zealand wines.
meals.dinner: The Sandfly Café, Te Anau — a casual but excellent local favourite for a relaxed dinner after a long day, known for hearty New Zealand comfort food.

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Sound road can be congested in peak season — departing early from Te Anau is essential. The drive itself is extraordinarily scenic. Weather at Milford Sound is famously changeable; rain actually enhances the experience with hundreds of temporary waterfalls. Book the premium cruise well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Kepler Track day hike — one of New Zealand's Great Walks, accessible directly from Te Anau. Take the water taxi across Lake Te Anau to Brod Bay and hike up through beech forest to the stunning alpine ridge section with panoramic views over Fiordland. The Luxmore Hut section offers world-class alpine scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the ridge toward Mt Luxmore if fitness allows, before descending back to Te Anau. The full day hike covers approximately 18–22km depending on how far you venture.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Te Anau on your final night in Fiordland.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast — depart for the water taxi by 8:00am.
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet trail lunch arranged by the lodge — enjoy at the Luxmore Hut with sweeping alpine views.
meals.dinner: Fiordland Lodge Restaurant — if staying at Fiordland Lodge, their in-house restaurant offers an exceptional dinner with locally sourced venison, salmon, and New Zealand wines in a stunning lakeside setting.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kepler Track water taxi in advance. November conditions on the alpine ridge can be exposed — carry layers, sunscreen, and rain gear. The ridge section is one of the finest alpine walks in New Zealand.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic drive back toward Queenstown via the Kingston Flyer route, stopping at Lake Hayes for a peaceful morning walk around the lake (approximately 8km loop). The lake is famous for its mirror-like reflections of the Remarkables and surrounding hills — a photographer's paradise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Queenstown for a final afternoon. Revisit favourite spots, do any last-minute luxury shopping, or enjoy a relaxing afternoon at the ONSEN Hot Pools for a final soak with gorge views.
day_by_day.evening: Premium farewell dinner in Queenstown — the finest meal of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast in Te Anau before checkout.
meals.lunch: Chard Farm Winery, Gibbston — stop at this stunning cliff-edge winery on the drive back for a wine tasting and light lunch platter overlooking the Kawarau River gorge.
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant by Josh Emmett — return for a final celebratory dinner, ordering from the full degustation menu with matched New Zealand wines. This is consistently rated among the finest dining experiences in the South Island.

day_by_day.notes: Lake Hayes is approximately 15 minutes from Queenstown — a perfect morning stop. Chard Farm is just off State Highway 6 near Gibbston. Book the farewell dinner at Rata well in advance and inform them it is a special occasion.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown — leisurely breakfast and a last walk along the Queenstown waterfront. Visit the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (approximately 2 hours return, gentle gradient) for one final elevated view over the lake and town as a farewell to the South Island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Queenstown Boutique Stay. Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final coffee and pastry at a lakeside café before private transfer to Queenstown Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Queenstown — carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days across one of the world's most spectacular landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Final in-hotel breakfast at Queenstown Boutique Stay — take your time and savour it.
meals.lunch: Eichardt's Bar, Queenstown — the iconic heritage hotel bar on the lakefront offers excellent light lunches and is the perfect final Queenstown dining experience.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight — N/A depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange checkout and airport transfer the evening before. Allow at least 2 hours before departure for airport check-in. Consider purchasing Central Otago Pinot Noir at the airport duty free as a premium souvenir of the trip.

query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026
